extracted.intended_audience: employers/regulated establishments, industry stakeholders, regulatory analysts, and public commenters on the OSHA heat standard NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the proposed OSHA requirements and economic-analysis conventions related to training and recordkeeping under the Heat Injury and Illness Prevention proposed standard, including who must be trained, training frequencies/types, recordkeeping obligations, and the cost-estimation assumptions and presentation conventions used in the NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory training on heat-related hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: All affected establishments would be required to provide training on heat-related hazards to at-risk workers and designated persons both upon promulgation and periodically thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline training obligation in the proposed standard; the text frames it as applying to 'at-risk workers' and 'designated persons' and occurring initially (upon promulgation) and periodically (refresher/supplemental) thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required training types and audiences (initial, annual refresher, supplemental; employees, designated persons, supervisors, at-risk workers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal specifies multiple training types: initial employee training (with subcategories for designated person and at-risk worker), initial supervisor training (development; supervisor; designated person), annual employee refresher training (designated person, at-risk worker), annual supervisor refresher training (supervisor, designated person), and supplemental employee refresher trainings (designated person, at-risk worker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables in the NPRM break out costs and counts by each specific training type and audience (e.g., 'Initial Employee Training—At-Risk Worker', 'Initial Supervisor Training—Supervisor', 'Annual Employee Refresher Training—Designated Person', 'Supplemental Employee Refresher Training—At-Risk Worker'), implying each is a distinct required or modelled training obligation under the proposed standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-estimation method for training (unit cost application)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA calculates total costs of each training requirement by either multiplying the number of affected establishments by the corresponding unit costs or multiplying the number of affected employees by the corresponding unit costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM distinguishes between establishment-based unit costs (developing, preparing, conducting employee training and supervisor training) and employee-based unit costs (initial, annual refresher, and supplemental trainings). Use the appropriate population (establishments vs employees) when applying unit costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of unit costs as establishment-based vs employee-based
rubrics_metrics.description: The unit costs to undergo employee trainings (initial, annual refresher, and supplemental) are employee-based and are combined with the number of affected employees. All other training-related unit costs are establishment-based (developing, preparing, conducting employee training (initial, annual refresher, supplemental) and supervisor training (initial, annual refresher)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When estimating costs, analyst should treat training-development and supervisor-training preparation/conduct as establishment-level activities and direct employee participation costs as per-employee; tables and totals in the NPRM follow this split.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental-training incidence assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA assumes that one percent of affected establishments would incur the establishment-based cost of supplemental trainings annually. Additionally, OSHA assumes employers would incur the cost of providing supplemental training to one percent of employees annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit modelling assumption for estimating recurring supplemental training costs; commenters or alternative analyses should note if they adopt a different incidence rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirement for environmental measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed standard would require affected indoor establishments to maintain environmental measurements for six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA assumes certain environmental monitoring equipment can automatically upload measurements to a recordkeeping database. Time to take measurements is accounted for elsewhere in the Identifying Heat Hazards provision, and OSHA assumes no additional maintenance-recordkeeping cost beyond that time (because of the assumed logger purchase captured elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption about monitoring equipment purchase and related costs
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA assumes establishments required to maintain records would purchase a wireless temperature and humidity data logger with automatic upload capability (cost captured under the Identifying Heat Hazards provision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because logger purchase costs are captured under another provision, OSHA assumes there is no additional separate cost to maintain the measurements beyond the time required to take them (time cost captured in Identifying Heat Hazards section). Analysts should avoid double-counting logger costs if following OSHA's allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis discounting and presentation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA presents costs discounted at 2 percent over a 10-year period and also shows undiscounted (0%) figures. Cost outputs are shown as one-time annualized, periodic costs annualized, annual costs, cost savings, and total annualized costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables display both 0% and 2% discount-rate columns and separate one-time annualized, annual, and total annualized costs. OSHA reports aggregate totals (e.g., annualized 2% total of $7.8 billion) and disaggregates by industry category and region. Analyses should mirror these presentation categories for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaggregation of cost estimates by industry category and region
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA reports cost estimates by industry category (e.g., Commercial Kitchens, Construction, Transportation, Non‑Core, etc.) and by geographic region (Alaskan, Central, Eastern, Pacific, Southern, Western), with subtotals and totals presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM tables break out one-time, annualized, annual, and total annualized costs per industry/region cell and provide subtotals and overall totals. Stakeholders should reference the appropriate industry-region cell when assessing burden or commenting on impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding and tabulation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: Due to rounding, figures in the columns and rows may not sum to the totals shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users of the tables should be aware small discrepancies may result from rounding; this is an explicit caveat in the NPRM tables.
